0.long_answer: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a neurodegenerative disease characterized by the progressive loss of both upper and lower motor neurons. This degeneration leads to muscle weakness, atrophy, and ultimately paralysis as the brain loses the ability to initiate and control voluntary movements. ALS is classified alongside other neurodegenerative diseases such as multiple sclerosis and Parkinson’s disease. It is also widely known as Lou Gehrig’s disease, named after the famous baseball player whose diagnosis brought public attention to the condition. The disease is typically fatal and currently has no cure, with treatment primarily focused on managing symptoms and slowing progression.
